Last week, Apple reported that its iPad revenue for the June quarter fell 5% year-over-year. Now, a new report puts that decline into the broader context of the tablet market in Q2 2026. Here are the details.

Global tablet shipments decline

According to a new report from research firm Omdia (cited by MacMagazine), global tablet shipments fell to 35.5 million units in Q2 2026, down 9.9% year-over-year.

The report noted that despite a 7.5% drop in shipments, Apple remained the market leader, shipping 13.5 million iPads with a 37.8% market share. Samsung followed with 5.8 million shipments and a 16.3% share; Lenovo ranked third with 11.1%, Xiaomi fourth with 8%, and Huawei fifth with 7.7%.

Lenovo was the only brand among the top five suppliers to post growth, with shipments up 27.1% compared to Q2 2025.

Omdia noted that suppliers outside the top five accounted for a combined 19.1% of shipments, with their total shipments down 23.5% year-over-year.

Below is Omdia research manager Himani Mukka's response to the report:

Mukka added that amid ongoing component supply tightness, "suppliers are unlikely to broadly prioritize tablets." Instead, they expect to "concentrate limited resources on flagship and premium models, further tilting their product mix toward higher-end devices."
